# Capabilities in delfin/agent/ that the PRODUCT does not reach.
#
# Written by tests/test_every_capability_has_a_caller.py, which refuses a
# name that is not in here. Columns: tier, name, where it is defined.
#
# tier "nowhere"   -- nothing in delfin/ or tests/ names it at all. Dead
#                     code, or a capability that was never connected.
# tier "test-only" -- only the suite reaches it. The capability exists and
#                     is proven, and nothing in the running product uses
#                     it.
#
# A name LEAVES this list by being connected or deleted, and the test then
# requires the list to be shortened: the count only goes down. Adding a
# line is a deliberate act and belongs in a pull request of its own, with
# the reason.
#
# Measured 2026-11-20, by the functions in that test file, so the list
# and the check cannot compute it differently.

# NOT removed 2026-11-22 (wave 36 c1, re-measured): there are two
# category vocabularies for one job. The product's compaction record
# carries its loss under the key ``lost`` in working_state's four
# categories (compaction_log.LOSS_CATEGORIES: denials, tests, files,
# instructions); category_names() is a second, broader keep-list list
# (goal, instruction, constraints, refusals, decisions, waits, tests)
# whose only reader would be a consumer of quality_report, which is
# itself unmounted one row below. Reporting a metric in this vocabulary
# would make five of its seven categories None forever, so the mount
# attempted here was withdrawn; the loss metric reports in the writer's
# vocabulary instead. Deciding which of the two lists the product should
# keep is a design decision, not a repair.
